package_info.why_malicious: The ATMZOW Magecart script is malicious because it injects unauthorized JavaScript into Magento CMS payment and donation pages, covertly harvesting sensitive payment and donor information (such as credit card numbers, names, expiration dates, and CVVs) and exfiltrating this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This compromises the confidentiality of user data and enables large-scale financial theft.

execution_context.trigger: When a user submits a payment or donation form on the Magento CMS frontend
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the payment/donation page template or inline script block in the Magento CMS frontend
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form field values
Network access to initiate outbound HTTPS requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user submits a payment or donation form, the code collects credit card and personal information from specific form fields in the DOM, serializes this data, and sends it via an outbound HTTPS POST request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in the exfiltration of sensitive payment credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously harvests sensitive payment and personal information directly from form fields and transmits it to an external, untrusted domain without user consent or legitimate business purpose. This behavior is characteristic of Magecart skimming attacks and is not present in legitimate payment workflows.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate payment pages should only transmit sensitive payment data to trusted, PCI-compliant payment processors or gateways, never to unknown or hardcoded third-party domains. Any script accessing payment fields and sending data externally is a severe violation of security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment integrations may collect form data, but only transmit it to authorized, well-known endpoints (such as Stripe or PayPal) and never collect full card details for external transmission. Any collection of full card data by frontend JavaScript is highly unusual outside of secure payment processor integrations.
key_indicators: JavaScript code accessing and reading credit card and personal data from DOM input fields on payment pages
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded, untrusted external domains from payment or donation pages
Injected or obfuscated JavaScript present in payment/donation page templates or inline script blocks
Execution of data exfiltration logic specifically during payment or donation form submission events

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects the ATMZOW Magecart JavaScript skimmer into the Magento CMS payment or donation page template, either by exploiting a vulnerability or compromising the CMS backend.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded and executed in the browsers of site visitors accessing payment or donation pages.

attack_chain.action: The injected JavaScript monitors the payment or donation form. When a user submits the form, it collects sensitive payment and personal information from the relevant input fields in the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Harvested payment and donor data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is serialized and sent via an outbound HTTPS POST request to an attacker-controlled domain specified in the script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and donor information, enabling financial fraud and data compromise.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code on payment or donation pages that accesses and reads credit card or personal data from form fields
Outbound network requests (especially HTTPS POST) from payment pages to hardcoded or untrusted external domains not associated with legitimate payment processors
Unexpected or unauthorized script injection or modification in Magento CMS frontend templates, especially in payment-related pages
file_indicators: Injected or obfuscated JavaScript code present in payment/donation page templates (e.g., app/design/frontend/*/template/checkout/*.phtml)
Unusual <script> tags or inline event handlers in Magento CMS files that are not part of the original codebase
Presence of unfamiliar or suspicious JavaScript files loaded on payment or donation pages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from payment or donation pages to domains not associated with legitimate payment processors (e.g., 'https://attacker-domain.com/collect')
Connections to known Magecart command-and-control (C2) infrastructure or previously identified malicious domains
Unusual network activity originating from payment page endpoints during form submission
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Magento CMS payment and donation page templates for unauthorized JavaScript modifications or obfuscated code. Inspect network traffic from payment pages for POST requests to unknown or untrusted domains, especially during form submission events. Use file integrity monitoring to detect changes in key frontend templates, and employ web application firewalls or content security policies to block unauthorized script execution and outbound data exfiltration.
